plan.title: Add directives collapsible to VSCode extension
plan.overview: Implement a new DIRECTIVES section in the VSCode sidebar that displays workflow/skill-to-directive mappings from config.yaml. Following the existing architecture, create a new domain orchestrator (directives.orchestrator.ts) that composes a view capability and config computer. Each workflow appears as a collapsible row that expands to show its assigned directives as clickable children that open the XML files.

approach.rationale:
Following three existing patterns from the codebase:
1. **Collapsible TreeItem Pattern** (tasks-view.capability.ts:16-51): StatusGroupItem shows how to create collapsible parent items with ThemeIcons and child counts. WorkflowItem will follow this exact pattern.
2. **Domain Orchestrator Pattern** (config.orchestrator.ts:55-118): The config orchestrator demonstrates a minimal orchestrator with TreeDataProvider, refresh, and file watcher. The directives orchestrator will follow this structure but add config parsing via a computer.
3. **Factory DI Pattern** (tasks-view.capability.ts:251-253): Capabilities use factory functions with explicit Deps interfaces. DirectivesViewCapability will follow this injection pattern.
The directives section is a distinct domain (separate data source: config.yaml directives section, separate concerns: directive visibility and file navigation) so it warrants its own orchestrator per coding directive principle A4.

task.name: Create directives view capability
task.requirements: FR1, FR2, FR3, FR4, FR5, FR6, FR7
task.action:
- Create WorkflowItem class extending vscode.TreeItem - Collapsible state: Collapsed (has directives) or None (empty) - Icon: new vscode.ThemeIcon('symbol-method') for workflow - Label: displayName from Workflow - Description: directive count or "No directives" for empty - contextValue: 'workflow'
- Create DirectiveItem class extending vscode.TreeItem - Collapsible state: None (leaf node) - Icon: exists ? ThemeIcon('symbol-ruler') : ThemeIcon('warning') - Label: directive name - Tooltip: exists ? undefined : "Directive file not found: {path}" - command: exists ? openFile command : undefined (FR6, FR7) - contextValue: 'directive' or 'directive-missing'
- Create factory function createDirectivesViewCapability(deps) - deps.loadWorkflows: () => Workflow[] - Returns TreeDataProvider with: - getChildren(element?): WorkflowItem[] at root, DirectiveItem[] for workflow - getParent(element): for reveal support - onDidChangeTreeData: EventEmitter for refresh - Cache workflows to avoid reloading - Parent tracking Map for getParent()
Target WorkflowItem: ```typescript export class WorkflowItem extends vscode.TreeItem { constructor(public readonly workflow: Workflow) { const hasDirectives = workflow.directives.length > 0; super( workflow.displayName, hasDirectives ? vscode.TreeItemCollapsibleState.Collapsed : vscode.TreeItemCollapsibleState.None ); this.iconPath = new vscode.ThemeIcon('symbol-method'); this.description = hasDirectives ? `${workflow.directives.length} directive${workflow.directives.length > 1 ? 's' : ''}` : 'No directives'; this.contextValue = 'workflow'; } } ```
task.done: Capability provides TreeDataProvider with WorkflowItem and DirectiveItem classes

testing.automated: None required - TreeView integration is VSCode UI, best verified manually. The computer could have unit tests but not strictly required for this scope.
testing.manual: - FR1: DIRECTIVES section visible in correct position - FR2: Workflows show as collapsible rows with chevron - FR3: Names formatted correctly (festina-scope -> Scope) - FR4: Empty workflows show "No directives" - FR5: Expanded workflow shows directives with symbol-ruler icon - FR6: Clicking directive opens XML file - FR7: Missing directive shows warning icon, click disabled - FR8: Modifying config.yaml or directive files triggers refresh
testing.regression: - Existing Config section still works - Product Docs and Engineering Docs still work - Tasks view still works - No impact on other domain orchestrators

pitfalls.pitfall: Use existing fast-xml-parser for XML, but config is YAML - use simple regex/line parsing or add js-yaml dependency. Check if YAML parsing exists elsewhere in codebase first.
Watch both directives/**/*.xml AND config.yaml to catch all changes that affect the view (FR8)
Use 'symbol-method' for workflows (skill/function), 'symbol-ruler' for directives (rules/guidelines), 'warning' for missing files - maintain consistency with VSCode conventions
Keep under 300 lines per coding directive - the directives orchestrator is simple enough to stay well under this limit
